def _drop_suspension_rows(bars):
    """A2a keeps trading-suspension rows as-is (open=high=low=0, volume=0, close
    = last reference price) rather than excluding the ticker - this is documented,
    deliberate upstream behavior (config/policies/price.v1.json: "거래정지와 장기
    공백은 정상 시장 사건이지 종목을 버릴 사유가 아니다", and its returnTransition
    block already requires volume>0 on both sides before treating two closes as a
    real price change).

    This engine has to make the same distinction at the row level: a halt row's
    open=0 cannot be a real entry fill, and its 0 high/low would inject a fake
    ~last_close-sized true-range spike into ATR. So these rows are dropped from
    the ticker's own series before indicators or execution ever see them - not a
    strategy filter (rule.py never sees this), just routing around a known upstream
    data artifact the same way price.v1.json's own consumers already do.
    """
    return bars[bars["volume"] > 0]

5_sourceUntouched.filterAppliesTo: an in-memory dict returned by A2aProvider.load() inside runner.run_smoke() only - the .cache/ parquet (provider-level cache) also stores the RAW pre-filter scan, confirmed separately below.

filterAppliedAtLines: bars_by_ticker = {t: _drop_suspension_rows(df) for t, df in bars_by_ticker_raw.items()}
6_singleApplicationPoint.note: bars_by_ticker is reassigned to the filtered result once, before the loop that calls rule.compute_features() (BB/CCI/ATR) and rule.generate_signals() (signal), and before build_order()/simulate_trade() (execution) - all four read the SAME already-filtered dict, not four separate filters that could drift apart.

evidence: strategies/5dc_v1a_p/rule.py never sees bars_raw - it only ever receives the already-filtered bars_by_ticker, and contains no reference to volume or suspension handling
the filter is defined and applied entirely inside engine/runner.py, upstream of rule.py - swapping strategies would inherit the same filtering with zero rule.py changes

price_v1_json_returnTransition.note: A2의 품질 검사와 A5의 수익률 계산이 '전이'를 같은 방식으로 정의하기 위한 공유 계약이다. 거래량 0인 날의 종가는 존재하지만 체결가가 아니므로(거래정지 중 기준가 표기) 수익률 계산에 쓰면 안 된다 — A2a에서 걷어낸 오염이 A5의 점수로 되돌아온다. A5는 이 블록을 읽어 체결이 있었던 날 사이에서만 수익률을 잰다.
price_v1_json_returnTransition.adjacencyNote: A5는 requireAdjacentTradingDay를 false로 쓴다. forward return은 d20/d60/d120처럼 거래일 인덱스 오프셋이라 인접 여부가 전제가 아니기 때문이다(BF-1.1 §5.3). A2의 일간 변동 검사만 인접을 요구한다 — 그쪽은 '하루 사이 변동'이 검사 대상이다. 두 용도의 차이는 여기서만 갈리고, volume>0 조건은 양쪽이 공유한다.

10_policyTextComparison.price_v1_json_qualityExclusion_reasonNot: 제외 사유 코드는 산출물에 남겨 A5가 그대로 노출할 수 있게 한다. 나중에 KRX·pykrx가 데이터를 고치면 특정 reason만 재검증하면 된다. ZERO_VOLUME_REFERENCE·LONG_SUSPENSION은 여기 없다 — 거래정지와 장기 공백은 정상 시장 사건이지 종목을 버릴 사유가 아니며, 진단 카운터(zeroVolumeTransitions·suspendedGapTransitions)로만 남긴다.
10_policyTextComparison.myPredicate: bars[bars['volume'] > 0]  -- unconditionally DROPS the row from the ticker's series
10_policyTextComparison.priceV1Json_actualMechanism: requireBothVolumePositive:true scoped to a PAIRWISE 'returnTransition' check (A2a/A2b/A5 consumers only) - it does NOT delete rows; it excludes a transition PAIR from return/quality calculations while the row itself remains in the dataset (reasonNote explicitly states: '거래정지와 장기 공백은... 종목을 버릴 사유가 아니며, 진단 카운터로만 남긴다').
10_policyTextComparison.verdict: BLOCKER-adjacent finding: price.v1.json defines NO literal predicate for this scenario (rolling technical-indicator computation). Its consumers list is [A2a, A2b, A5] - a Strategy Lab indicator engine is not among them, and the policy's own mechanism (pairwise transition exclusion, row preserved) is architecturally different from row deletion. This filter is therefore a NEW design decision for a scenario the existing policy does not cover, not a reuse of an existing rule - reported as such rather than asserting an equivalence that doesn't hold byte-for-byte.
